label: GO after a1 -> S2 unrewarded; larger when belief favours S1, early episode
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) ;; (phase == GO) * ep_dec
explanation: Fires only at GO (zero at D1 and D2). Magnitude is set mainly by the previous trial being a1 -> S2 (rare) unrewarded (weight ~+1.27; residual +0.69 vs about -0.08 for every other pattern; a2 S2 u adds only ~+0.02-0.04). Within those trials it grows with the ideal-observer log-odds that S1 is good (belief_lo, ~+0.13 per unit) and shrinks with episode decile (~-0.21 per decile). On a window first trial, where the previous pattern is unknown but prev_reward = 0 is visible, it fires partly (+0.37) with the same belief/ep_dec modulation, presumably reflecting the a1 S2 u trials that fall outside the window. Generic GO and GO*ep_dec terms soak up the timing baseline offset, which is otherwise spread over all GO steps. Belief deciles on their own score just 0.09 and the hidden good state / trials since reversal ~0. Only observed quantities are used (no value/policy and no future variables). Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.75 vs the profile ceilings of all observed 0.44 and all 0.51; these terms go past the additive ceiling because they use interactions. Leaving out the model value/policy costs little here, since belief_lo times the a1 S2 u pattern stands in for the graded part.

issues: The core claims hold up. I reproduced the scores (dev 0.753, test 0.7485). GO is the only phase where it fires: the D1 and D2 residuals are all 0. The a1 S2 u residual is +0.689 and every other pattern sits near -0.08. The weights are +1.42 for a1 S2 u, +0.129 for belief_lo and -0.232 for ep_dec.

The explanation misreads the a2 S2 u case. Its mean residual is only +0.019 because it is bimodal by belief, and misses ranks 'GO after a2 S2 u' as the most under-predicted cell (+0.084). Several worst-fit windows fire strongly after a2 S2 u when the agent goes on to choose a1 (actual 1.81 vs predicted 0.05; 1.74 vs 0.03), and it builds up over repeated a2 S2 u trials (0.42 -> 0.88 -> 1.36). Adding (GO)*last_is('a2 S2 u')*max(belief_lo,0) to the 8-term set raises test R^2 beyond timing to 0.80. So a2 S2 u when belief favours S1 is a real secondary driver. The label leaves it out and the explanation dismisses it.

The label gets the ranking of modulators wrong. Episode position matters much more than belief. Test R^2 is 0.43 with no modulators, 0.457 adding only the belief_lo terms, and 0.717 adding only the ep_dec terms. Yet the label leads with 'larger when belief favours S1'.
The effect of episode position fits better as a decay to zero than as a straight line. Using max(1.5 - 0.2*ep_dec, 0) as the gain raises test from 0.749 to 0.755.
Minor point: the window-first ep_dec term is not redundant. Dropping it lowers test R^2 to 0.729. The explanation's account of the window-first case is plausible.
